This article first appeared on GuruFocus.

International Business Machines (NYSE:IBM) shares climbed 3.33% to $243.47 at the 4:00 p.m. ET close on November 25, after Wedbush started coverage with an Outperform rating and a $276 price target. The gain came against a 0.62% drop in the Nasdaq Composite. Shares opened at $233.50 and traded near $245.25 in the afternoon, up about 5% from the open at that point.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 8 Warning Signs with SOBKY.

Is IBM fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

IBM GF Value chart

Wedbush's Moshe Katri set the new marker after a third quarter in which IBM beat expectations on both lines. Adjusted earnings came in at $2.95 a share against $2.85 expected, and revenue reached $17.10 billion against $16.82 billion. The timing helped. On a day when investors dumped AI hardware names over spending fears, IBM's mix of software, consulting and mainframes may have looked like a way to own AI demand without funding a data center buildout.

The $276 target sits 13.4% above the close, a reasonable gap for a mature company rather than a growth bet. The GuruFocus chart shows a GF Score of 79/100, with steady profitability and momentum held back by a balance sheet that ranks only middling. GF Value is $248.84, a 2.2% discount, and GuruFocus rates the shares fairly valued, so the rally has closed most of the model's gap and leaves little cushion. The next test is fourth-quarter software growth in January, which will show whether IBM's AI bookings turn into revenue fast enough to justify the higher price.

title: Standard Chartered unit reports customer data breach
detail:
Standard Chartered unit reports customer data breach
Arjun Parashar
Thu, November 26, 2026 at 11:30 AM EST 3 min read
STAN.L
IBM
Trade IBM on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Keeping customer data safe is hard for banks. Even the biggest names struggle with it.

A breach at a financial firm costs $6.3 million on average, per IBM's July 29 report. Across all industries, the average is $4.99 million.

On Nov. 19, JPMorgan Chase said hackers got into marketing data held by its vendors. That data may include customer names and email addresses.

Now, seven days later, Zodia Custody, a crypto custodian that Standard Chartered agreed to buy in October, has reported its own data breach.

Related: Bitcoin miners bet big on AI. Now, one is down 70%

What happened at Zodia Custody?

Zodia Custody CEO Richard Clark told Reuters that the company detected the breach on Monday, Nov. 23.

The incident exposed some client and employee information, including names and email addresses.

However, Zodia did not disclose how many people were affected or how attackers gained access to the information.

The report also did not establish whether any cryptocurrency holdings were compromised.

Zodia is a crypto custodian. Think of it as a vault for digital assets. Big institutions, such as funds and banks, use it to store their crypto.

It keeps their private keys safe. These keys are what allow someone to move the crypto.

Trending on TheStreet Roundtable:

Cathie Wood scraps plans for two new crypto ETFs

Grand Theft Auto VI outplays Nvidia and SpaceX

Bitcoin rallies as Nvidia brings back Jensen Huang

Zodia is not an exchange. A custodian's main job is to guard assets, not to trade them. It runs regulated entities in Singapore, Hong Kong, Australia, the UAE and Luxembourg.

Standard Chartered agreed to buy Zodia in a deal announced on Oct. 21.

Although the reported breach involved personal information, exposed contact details could potentially be used in phishing attacks targeting institutional clients.

Recent cyberattacks hit banks and crypto exchanges

The incident follows several major security breaches across the financial sector. Zodia isn't the first financial firm to report a breach lately.

A week earlier, on Nov. 19, JPMorgan Chase disclosed that attackers had accessed customer marketing data held by third-party vendors. The exposed information could include names and email addresses.

Crypto firms have faced similar data breaches before. 

In May 2025, Coinbase disclosed that attackers had bribed overseas support personnel to obtain customer information. The stolen data included names, contact details, bank account information and government identification documents.

Coinbase said no passwords, private keys or customer funds were directly compromised.

Shares of Kyndryl Holdings KD), a 2021 IBM IBM) spinoff, have held up well amid the broader tech selloff as investors respond to improving profitability.

At around $16 a share, KD stock still looks attractively valued after climbing more than 20% since reporting strong results for its fiscal second quarter earlier this month.

Zacks Investment Research

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

What Does Kyndryl Do?

Kyndryl manages the IT infrastructure that large organizations rely on for day-to-day operations, from mainframes and data centers to hybrid cloud environments. Through Kyndryl Consult, it also helps clients modernize applications, strengthen cybersecurity, and put AI to work in existing systems.

Kyndryl's Earnings Outlook Is Improving

Fiscal Q2 showed how Kyndryl can grow earnings even when sales soften. Revenue fell nearly 2% year over year to $3.65 billion, but adjusted pretax income climbed 22% to $150 million and Q2 adjusted EPS rose to $0.42 from $0.38. Furthermore, Kyndryl exceeded Q2 sales and EPS expectations of $3.6 billion and $0.37 per share by over 1% and 13%, respectively.

This comes as analysts still expect annual sales to remain above $14 billion through fiscal 2029. The Zacks Consensus Estimate calls for Kyndryl's EPS to rise 33% to $1.94 in its current FY27 and another 26% to $2.45 in FY28.

Zacks Investment Research

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Reassuringly, over the past 30 days, FY27 and FY28 EPS estimates have risen more than 4%. Near-term estimates have also risen, with the Q3 EPS consensus up to $0.80 from $0.76 in the last month and the Q4 EPS estimate up to $0.82 from $0.80.

Zacks Investment Research

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

KD's Enticing Valuation

At current levels, KD shares trade at just 8X forward earnings and at less than 1X forward sales. Those are attractive multiples for a tech stock with double-digit earnings growth projected for fiscal 2027 and 2028, offering a more than 50% discount to the forward P/E averages of the benchmark S&P 500 and its Zacks Technology Services Industry. 

Zacks Investment Research

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Bottom Line

In addition to sporting a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), Kyndryl Holdings stock checks an overall "A" VGM Zacks Style Scores grade for its combination of Value, Growth, and Momentum.

Although KD would be an ideal buy-the-dip target amid broader market weakness, rising earnings estimates and a modest valuation suggest there could still be meaningful upside from here.

title: What's Behind Dell Stock's Fall?
detail:
What's Behind Dell Stock's Fall?
Trefis Team

^GSPC
HPE
CSCO
HPQ

Trading disclosure

Today's big story: Anthropic Below Its IPO Price: Do Giants Come Back?

Dell Technologies stock fell 11.8% on Tuesday, Nov 24, to close at $295.28. The S&P 500 slipped 0.5% the same session.

The fall was not a reaction to Dell's results. The company reported after the closing bell that day. The stock fell with most of its group, but further. Ten of the eleven other technology hardware companies worth $2 billion or more ended lower.

Did Dell's Results Cause The Fall?

No. Dell released results for its fiscal third quarter, the three months to October 2026, after Tuesday's close. Revenue was a record $54.9 billion, up 103% from a year earlier. Analysts had expected about $49.3 billion.

Adjusted earnings per share were $9.45. That figure leaves out some costs. Analysts had expected $6.62, so both revenue and adjusted earnings beat estimates.

Dell rose 20.5% on Monday, then fell 11.8% on Tuesday. Swings that size are hard to sit through when one stock holds a big part of the savings you live on. The Trefis Income Solution pays a dividend yield about 3 times the S&P 500's, from 50 companies that have paid dividends for at least 10 years in a row. See what it pays.

Was It Dell Or Its Group?

Dell fell with its group, but much further. Of the 11 other technology hardware companies worth $2 billion or more, 10 fell and 1 rose.

Their median move was a fall of 7.2%, while Dell fell 11.8%. Eight of them fell 5% or more.

Broader measures fell less. XLK, a fund that tracks the technology sector, fell 3.3%. The Nasdaq Composite index fell 1.5%.

On the Trefis peer list for Dell, three companies fell and two rose. HP, Hewlett Packard Enterprise and Cisco Systems fell. International Business Machines and Apple rose. Cisco and IBM are not among the 11 companies counted above.

Hewlett Packard Enterprise fell 16.3%, more than Dell. Before Tuesday's session, it raised its outlook, but its shares fell on worries about its margins.

Where Does Dell Stock Stand Now?

In the year before Tuesday, Dell had one fall at least this large. Counting rises too, it had 8 moves at least this large. The latest was Monday's 20.5% rise.

Over the past year, Dell returned 143.6% including dividends. The S&P 500 returned 10.3% on the same basis. Over the past month, Dell lost 36.8% including dividends.

Its highest close of the past 12 months was $588.40, on Sept 17. Its lowest close of the past 12 months was $111.07, on Jan 20.

The next report covers Dell's fiscal fourth quarter, the three months to January 2027. It is due in February 2027. That report will show how much of Dell's backlog of AI server orders not yet shipped remains. Dell ended its third quarter with a record $132.3 billion of them.

title: IBM and Microsoft expand Azure Compute Fleet integration
detail:
IBM and Microsoft expand Azure Compute Fleet integration
The integration also allows organisations to use discounted Azure Spot VMs for fault-tolerant workloads. Credit: Erman Gunes / Shutterstock.com · Verdict · Erman Gunes / Shutterstock.com
Shubhendu Vimal
Wed, November 25, 2026 at 6:43 AM EST 2 min read
IBM
MSFT
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

IBM and Microsoft have expanded their collaboration with the general availability of IBM Spectrum LSF and IBM Spectrum Collective provider plug-ins for Microsoft Azure Compute Fleet.

The plug-ins connect IBM's workload orchestration software with Azure Compute Fleet for compute-intensive workloads across hybrid environments.

The integration is aimed at applications including electronic design automation, computer-aided engineering, genome sequencing, molecular dynamics, AI training, fine-tuning, data analytics and AI inference.

IBM Spectrum LSF and IBM Spectrum Collective distribute, deploy, orchestrate and optimise workloads across available computing resources.

With the Azure Compute Fleet integration, organisations can provision and release Azure virtual machines (VMs) automatically in response to workload requirements.

Users can specify several eligible Azure VM families and sizes through a single compute fleet request, including HDv2 and HXv2 instances.

This approach is intended to reduce dependence on one VM configuration and improve capacity availability during periods of high demand.

The integration also allows organisations to use discounted Azure Spot VMs for fault-tolerant workloads that can be restarted, while using pay-as-you-go capacity for workloads requiring more continuity.

Companies can add Azure capacity to process queued workloads during peak demand, then release those resources as demand declines.

IBM said the plug-ins enable existing on-premises IBM Spectrum LSF and Spectrum Collective installations to extend into Azure without altering existing job-submission workflows or application scheduling practices.

The companies developed the native integration together to support workload orchestration across on-premises infrastructure, hyperscale cloud platforms and neocloud environments.

Separately, Reuters reported that Microsoft has declared a "Code Red" drive to overhaul how it prevents and responds to major service failures after a 24-hour outage exposed shortcomings in its engineering systems and crisis response, citing internal memos.

The outage on 12-13 November affected governments from Australia and Japan to the US, delayed trading firms and disrupted airline communications.

Microsoft said the incident was not related to cyber activity or AI agents.

Microsoft attributed the outage to an undetected Windows scalability defect introduced in July.

Chief executive Satya Nadella publicly apologised for the disruption.

"IBM and Microsoft expand Azure Compute Fleet integration" was originally created and published by Verdict, a GlobalData owned brand.

title: Is IBM Stock Paying You Enough For The Swings?
detail:
Is IBM Stock Paying You Enough For The Swings?
Trefis Team
Wed, November 25, 2026 at 6:43 AM EST 4 min read
IBM
^GSPC
Trade IBM on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Image from Pixabay

Today's big story: Anthropic Below Its IPO Price: Do Giants Come Back?

You may hold International Business Machines (IBM) next to an S&P 500 index fund. Its mainframe, management says, runs 70% of the industry's transaction volume by value. A business that central can make IBM look like the calm part of your money. Every stock adds its own swings to the market's, and wider swings should earn you more. So, measured against the index, has IBM's return over the years made up for how much its shares jump around?

IBM's Swings Have Paid Slightly Better Than The Index's

IBM returned 19.0% a year with dividends from November 16, 2021, to November 24, 2026. That beat the S&P 500's 10.4%, but you took a bumpier ride for it. IBM's annual volatility, how far its price usually strays over a year, was 30.5%, against 17.4% for the index. Divide the return by the volatility and IBM earned 0.623 for each unit of swing. The index earned 0.598. So each bump in IBM's price has paid you a little more than the market's did, but only a little.

IBM's price has swung 30.5% a year, against 17.4% for the S&P 500. That means sitting through deeper drops in the money you keep in it. The Trefis Income Solution owns 50 companies that have each paid dividends for at least 10 years in a row, and together they yield about 3 times what the S&P 500 pays. See the Income Solution.

IBM On The S&P 500's Up And Down Days

In the past year, IBM lost more on the market's bad days than it gained on its good ones. From November 21, 2025, to November 24, 2026, a $10,000 holding in IBM gained $62.40 on an average day the S&P 500 rose. The same sum in the index gained $69.80. On an average down day, the IBM holding lost $74.30, against $65.30 in the index. That is an average, not a rule. On November 5, 2026, the index's worst day of the past year, the S&P 500 fell 4.4% and IBM fell 2.8%.

IBM's own swings were far wider than the market's. Its volatility over the past year was 48.5%, against 15.0% for the index. Yet for each 1% the S&P 500 moved, IBM moved only about 0.77% on average. Its daily moves tracked the index only loosely. Their correlation was 0.24, on a scale where 1 means moving in step. So IBM does not simply magnify the market for you. It adds big swings of its own.

What IBM's Business Says About The Swings Ahead

IBM has a steady core with a lumpy edge. That edge can swing software growth from one quarter to the next. The steady part is software that clients pay for every year. On the October 21, 2026, call, management said this annual recurring revenue grew 8% to $24.9 billion. For all of 2026, IBM expects revenue growth of 4% to 5% at constant currency.
